fullPassage: Charles Lyell (1797–1875), best known as the author of Principles of Geology, was born in Scotland to a wealthy family, the eldest of ten. Although he was called to the bar in 1822 at Lincoln’s Inn, his father’s financing allowed him to pursue his childhood love of nature and geology. He became Secretary of the Geological Society of London in 1823 and served as its president for two terms, traveling widely and studying geology not only in England but in France, Sicily, the Alps, the Canary Islands, and North America (from Nova Scotia to the Mississippi Delta).
